title: The seven decision points
objectives: List the seven decision points in a SIP's life.
Say which points keep the habit alive and which protect what it has built.
body_md:
A SIP is not a one-time decision. Over its life it passes through seven decision points, and most of the value we add comes from getting these right.

| # | Decision point | When it comes up | Our default stance |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Step-up | Every year, or after a raise | Raise the SIP by 5–10% a year if the budget allows |
| 2 | Pause | Short-term cash crunch | Pause briefly rather than stop or redeem |
| 3 | Missed instalments | Bank balance short on the debit date | Fix the mandate fast; repeated misses can cancel the SIP |
| 4 | Market fall | Any time | Keep going; this is when SIPs buy the most units |
| 5 | End date reached | The SIP's registered tenure ends | Renew if the goal is still years away |
| 6 | Goal 1–3 years away | Approaching the goal | Stop new equity money; start moving to debt gradually |
| 7 | Goal reached | The money is needed | Redeem in stages, or use an SWP for regular income |

## Two halves of the same life

Points 1 to 4 keep the habit alive: they are about paying more, skipping a month, fixing a mandate and not stopping in a fall. Points 5 to 7 protect what the habit has built: renewing, gliding down and drawing the money out.

Every one of the seven has a question to ask before acting. That is the next stage of the module.
example: A client calls to stop a SIP because the market fell 15%. That is point 4, not point 2 — the cash-flow review shows his salary is stable, so the answer is to keep going, not to pause.
say: There are seven decisions in a SIP's life, and each one has a default answer.
Points one to four keep the habit alive; points five to seven protect what it built.
never: The SIP is on autopilot, so nothing needs deciding.
Stopping is the same as pausing.

check.q: A client has a three-month cash crunch. Which decision point is this, and what is the default stance?
o: A pause; pause briefly rather than stop or redeem
check.why: A short cash crunch is decision point 2: pause briefly, and keep the SIP and the units intact.

check.q: Which decision point protects the money once the goal is close?
o: Goal 1–3 years away: move gradually to debt
check.why: Points 5 to 7 protect what the habit built; the glide path starts when the goal is one to three years away.

check.q: What is the default stance when a SIP's end date arrives and the goal is still years away?
check.why: If the goal is far, renew or extend the SIP and keep stepping it up.
